cost.description:
Regarding infrastructure costs: Digitization, Storage, Licensing, Sharing and Re-use and Archiving, it was estimated a cost of around 1000 Euros to acquire external hard drives to store backup data in addition to the local drives at the geotechnical centrifuge laboratory. Zenodo was selected as it has the advantage of being a free repository and offer a limit of 50GB per dataset.

Regarding skill costs that comprise data wrangling, description and documentation, metadata generation, formatting and cleaning it was estimated a cost in terms of time, leading to 2 days of work per month of the researcher Cristian Soriano.

data_quality_assurance: In the SHAREWIND project, we have established comprehensive procedures for quality assurance to ensure the integrity and reliability of our research data. These documented procedures encompass a range of practices aimed at validating the cleanliness, consistency, and overall quality of the data. To achieve this, we employ tools and scripts tailored to the specific characteristics of our dataset, enabling automated checks for duplicates, inconsistencies, and proper data structuring. Our quality assurance framework is designed to address potential errors at various stages of the data lifecycle, from collection to analysis. These procedures are documented in detail, outlining the specific checks performed, the tools utilized, and the criteria for data validation. Regular audits and reviews will be conducted to maintain the effectiveness of our quality assurance measures, providing confidence in the accuracy and reliability of the research data throughout the project's duration. Any updates or modifications to these procedures will be duly documented and communicated, ensuring transparency and adherence to best practices in research data management.
dataset.description:
The SHAREWIND project aims to generate comprehensive datasets through a combination of experiments and numerical simulations. The dataset will encompass various formats to capture the diverse nature of the research:

CSV (.csv) files: These files will contain measured data from sensors utilized in centrifuge experiments and data points derived from processed numerical models.

MP4 files: Video recordings of the experiments will be stored in this format, providing visual documentation of the research processes.

JPEG files: Images and photographs relevant to the experiments and simulations will be represented in JPEG format.

Text files (.txt): Metadata associated with the dataset will be stored in plain text files, providing essential information about the experimental setup and numerical models.

DXF files: Computer-assisted drawings of schemas will be documented in DXF format, facilitating a visual representation of experimental and numerical configurations.

PDF and .tex files: Text documents, including research reports and technical documentation, will be stored in both PDF and LaTeX (.tex) formats.

format:
The SHAREWIND project will generate data from experiments and numerical simulations. Non-proprietary format files will be produced to guarantee the interoperability and accessibility of the data. The generated data will be in the following formats:

CSV (.csv) files: Containing measured data from sensors in centrifuge experiments and data points of processed numerical models.

MP4 files: For video recordings of the experiments.

JPEG files: For images and photos.

Text files (.txt): For metadata.

DXF files: For computer-assisted drawings of schemas.

PDF and .tex files: For text documents.

host.description: The project repository for the SHAREWIND project will be on Zenodo. A community link has been created in Zenodo to organize all the outputs and publications associated with the project: https://zenodo.org/communities/sharewind.

distribution.title: SHAREWIND - Shared anchors for floating wind turbines

distribution.available_until: By choosing Zenodo, data is stored in the CERN Data Center. Both data files and metadata are kept in multiple independent replicas. The data will be preserved for at least 20 years in the data repository. This preservation duration exceeds the standard practices and aligns with the long-term commitment to accessibility and openness, ensuring that the SHAREWIND project's datasets remain available for an extended period after the project's completion. Researchers, practitioners, and other stakeholders will have sustained access to the dataset, fostering ongoing utilization and potential contributions to future research and applications.

metadata.description:
In the project repository, a comprehensive set of metadata will be included to describe the datasets and enhance their discoverability. The metadata will include the following elements:
Data Persistent ID (DOI): A unique identifier assigned to each dataset for citation and persistent access.

Publication Date: The date when the dataset is published or made publicly available.
Title: A concise and descriptive title that represents the content of the dataset.

Author(s): The individuals or entities responsible for creating the dataset.
Contact: Information about the person or entity to contact for inquiries or collaboration related to the dataset.

Description: A detailed narrative describing the content, context, and purpose of the dataset.

Subject: The main subject or topic covered by the dataset.

Keywords: Relevant keywords or phrases that aid in the discovery of the dataset.
Related Publication(s): Citations or references to publications related to the dataset.
Language: The language(s) in which the dataset is presented.

Producer: Information about the entity or person responsible for producing the dataset.

Deposit Date: The date when the dataset is deposited or made available in the repository.
Type of Data: A categorization indicating the nature or type of data represented in the dataset.

By including these metadata elements, we aim to provide a comprehensive and well-documented description of the datasets, fostering their accessibility and reuse within the research community.

dataset.preservation_statement: As previously mentioned, Zenodo guarantees storage for at least 20 years, ensuring a long-term preservation commitment. In addition to Zenodo, local copies of all datasets will be preserved on the Université Gustave Eiffel servers, providing an additional layer of security and redundancy. Furthermore, external hard drives will be kept in the laboratory facilities, serving as another measure to safeguard the datasets. These multi-tiered preservation policies and practices ensure the resilience and longevity of the described dataset/output, mitigating the risk of data loss and supporting sustained access for future research and use

security_and_privacy.description:
During the course of the research project, all data will be stored on local servers maintained and automatically backed up by the Université Gustave Eiffel. Every night, data will be automatically backed up, and recovery measures are in place through the Université Gustave Eiffel ICT services in the event of an accident. Access to the designated server is restricted to laboratory team members, including Cristian Soriano, Luc Thorel (project supervisor), and laboratory director Matthieu Blanc.
Additionally, datasets will be stored in the Université Gustave Eiffel cloud service, where access is granted using university identifiers and passwords. The cloud service serves as an additional backup and an alternative for online access to datasets.

After the project, the datasets will be published in Zenodo with an open access license CC-BY, ensuring continued security measures and accessibility for broader use and dissemination.

dmp.description: This document describes the lifecycle of the data to be collected, processed, and generated by the SHAREWIND project. It provides a summary of anticipated data types, formats, and structures, detailing the considerations and strategies to implement FAIR data principles. The current Data Management Plan includes a data summary, considerations for making data FAIR, details on other research outputs, allocation of resources, data security, ethics, and other relevant issues. The Data Management Plan for the SHAREWIND project is a dynamic document that will be updated throughout the development of the project. This version of the document represents the first submission of the Data Management Plan in December 2023.
